<reason>Both sides were competent and the clash was well-defined, but PRO controlled the decisive axis. PRO's early separation of "when" from "whether itemized" defused CON's strongest structural argument ([B1.4]) and converted it into support for early disclosure. PRO then answered CON's best objection — that fees are not knowable before payment — with the rate-card mechanism (state fixed amounts as numbers, variable ones as their governing rule, compute when inputs exist), which directly rebuts the "false precision/whiplash" line without requiring guesses; CON never showed why stating a seller-authored formula early is inaccurate, only that it is less convenient to compare. CON's reply that formulas are "homework" was its best counter, but PRO's rejoinder — that a diner choosing a restaurant needs to know an 18% mandatory charge exists, not the final cents — was more responsive to how the decision actually gets made. CON's [B4.1] concession that flat service charges and per-ticket schedules are already routinely posted undercut its own defense of the final screen, and PRO harvested that cleanly in closing. CON's worker/context argument also drifted toward conceding PRO's core claim (that early visibility would deter customers), which PRO's Q2 exposed and CON's answer ("not sight but sight without the room") only partly repaired. Both sides used proper A1:/A2: labeling and stayed grounded without fake citations. PRO takes a small execution hit for the clipped first rebuttal, but the lost material was marginal. CON's "you can still walk away" defense remained the softest point in its case after PRO's sunk-cost pressure.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's Rebuttal 2 [A4.1]-[A4.3]: answering that no estimate need be wrong because fixed charges are stated as numbers and variable ones as rules, and conditional charges disclosed conditionally at the moment the condition attaches. This dissolved CON's central "early means inaccurate, or means clutter for everyone" dilemma and forced CON into defending the final screen for even flat, seller-set charges — a position it then partly conceded in [B4.1].</best_rebuttal>
